page_title: Graph Convolutional Network Layer Mechanics and Graph Classification
summary: This page details the mathematical formulation of Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) layers, specifically focusing on the update rules for node embeddings through neighborhood aggregation and linear transformation. It contrasts the 'vanilla' GCN approach with enhanced versions that include learnable self-loops or separate self-transformation weights. The lecture concludes by demonstrating how these sequential layers are utilized for graph-level tasks, such as graph classification, using a readout function and an MLP classifier.

parsed.page_title: Graph Convolutional Network Layer Mechanics and Graph Classification
parsed.summary: This page details the mathematical formulation of Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) layers, specifically focusing on the update rules for node embeddings through neighborhood aggregation and linear transformation. It contrasts the 'vanilla' GCN approach with enhanced versions that include learnable self-loops or separate self-transformation weights. The lecture concludes by demonstrating how these sequential layers are utilized for graph-level tasks, such as graph classification, using a readout function and an MLP classifier.

concepts.evidence: Introducing layer-wise non-linearity and biases into GCN
node embeddings (stored in columns of X)

applying the same linear transformation Ω0 to the aggregated nodes
